label: early original-phase steps (t<=2) on input e or right after e/t/w
explanation: Fires almost only in the first three original-phase steps (t=0..2 carry ~96% of activation mass; t=1 alone ~48%). Never fires at the delimiter, and copy-phase activity is tiny (~2% of mass). Within t<=2 it is driven by the token e: input e has 14x lift (~47% of mass), and the step right after e, t, or w (prev_tok lift 7x/5x/4x) also fires. The strongest activations come from runs of e at the start: "t e e" gives the max at the second e, and "e e e" ramps 0.19 -> 0.68 -> 0.97 of max. A lone e at t=0 gives a small, fixed ~0.19 of max. Predicate: t<=2 and (input is e, or the previous input is e/t/w). It captures ~91% of mass but has low precision (~0.37), because many steps after t/w (and some e steps) stay inactive depending on the current token. Misses (~9% of mass) are mostly an e at t=3 after an earlier e, plus scattered weak copy-phase activations late in long sequences.
